sam: Heads-up — after merging the stream-priority refactor I'm hitting repeat comm/compute stalls on multi-GPU runs. Repro steps included below.

sam: Repro config: tp=2 pp=1 batch=8, model=redwood-small, nightly runner. Problem shows up on shard-2 consistently.

sam: nvprof / CUPTI shows kernel launches on compute stream get blocked waiting for an event from the NCCL stream. Seems like event ordering not honored when CUDA graphs are captured.

sam: Minimal run command: `./run_infer --model redwood-small --tp 2 --batch 8 --profile nvtx --use-graphs=true`

 sam: snippet of logs (trimmed):
 ```
 [epoch] capture: begin cuda graph capture on stream 0
 [nccl] ncclAllReduce start on stream 1
 [nccl] ncclAllReduce done
 [event] recorded event e123 on stream 1
 [compute] kernel launch queued on stream 0, waiting on e123
 [cuda] graph replay -> kernel stuck at sync waiting on event
 ```

 rika: Can you paste the PR that landed the change? I want to see where streams are created/assigned.

 sam: PR: https://git.redwood/infra/PR-8342 (stream ownership + priority plumbing). The refactor now creates dedicated high-priority streams and records events from the nccl thread into them.

 oliver: This rings a bell — we've seen issues where events recorded on a non-capture stream don't correctly serialize with a captured graph's dependencies. CUDA graphs have weird semantics: events recorded outside capture may not unblock nodes inside a captured graph unless the event is recorded on the capture stream or dependency is added to the graph.

 kmurray: Quick hypothesis: we record the event on the nccl stream, then capture the graph on compute stream; on replay the graph's internal nodes expect the event but the recorded event timeline doesn't match. Workaround: record the event on the capture/compute stream before ending capture, or add graph dependencies via `cudaGraphAddDependencies`.

 sam: Did a smoke test: forcing `cudaStreamSynchronize` right after nccl completes removes the stall (overlap lost, but no hang). Disabling graph capture (`--use-graphs=false`) also restores overlap correctly. So graph path is the culprit.

 perf-bot: perf alert: rolling benchmark shows ~12% p99 latency regression on tp=2 since PR-8342 landed. Regression detected on shards 1-3.

 rika: Good catch. Can we bisect to the exact line? If it's the event stream selection, maybe simplest fix is to record events on the capture stream or flip ordering when capturing.

 oliver: Also check whether we're using `cudaEventRecord` with the correct flags. Events created with default flags are fine but when used across graphs you need explicit graph dependencies. Another angle: are we using `cudaGraphAddChildGraphNode` anywhere? that can reorder streams.

 kmurray: I'll put up a quick patch: record events on the compute/capture stream when we need to sync compute to comm, and call `cudaGraphAddDependencies(graph, deps...)` to make the dependency explicit. If that proves flaky, fallback is to disable graphs for TP>1 until stable.

 infra-bot: CI: queued dedicated multi-gpu job for PR-8356 (kmurray/graph-deps) — run id: 9872. Will post results.

 sam: Thanks. I pushed a small repro to gist: https://gist.redwood/capture-graph-repro (includes nvtx timeline and small repro harness).

 rika: Assigning this to @kmurray. Please include a regression test in the perf harness that runs tp=2 with graphs on/off.

 kmurray: Will do. If CI confirms, plan: (1) add graph dependency fix, (2) add test, (3) add fallback flag `--force-disable-graphs-for-tp` to avoid customer impact.

 sam: Great — leaving the logs + nvtx traces in the gist. :thumbsup:
